B1-1-0.point: Relative pronouns as subjects and objects; pronoun omission
B1-1-0.title: Relative pronoun: subject or object?
B1-1-0.note_es: Si el pronombre relativo es el sujeto de la cláusula, no se puede omitir. Si es el objeto, puedes omitirlo.

B1-1-1.title: It + feeling + when clause
B1-1-1.note_es: It es un sujeto formal. Después va el sentimiento y when + oración, que dice cuándo ocurre.

B1-2-0.point: Gerund phrases as subjects and objects
B1-2-0.title: Gerund phrases
B1-2-0.note_es: Un gerundio (verbo + -ing) funciona como un nombre: puede ser sujeto, objeto de un verbo o objeto de una preposición.

B1-2-1.point: Comparisons with adjectives, nouns, verbs and past participles
B1-2-1.title: Comparing adjectives, nouns and verbs
B1-2-1.note_es: Los adjetivos usan -er/more... than. Los nombres usan more/fewer/less... than. Los verbos usan un adverbio comparativo: harder than.

B1-3-0.point: Requests with modals, if-clauses and gerunds
B1-3-0.title: Requests: how polite?
B1-3-0.note_es: Cada fórmula es más cortés que la anterior. Con Do you mind if I... y Would you mind... recuerda: if + sujeto + verbo; mind + -ing.

marks.ex: Do you mind if I sit here?

B1-3-1.title: Yes/no question to indirect: if
B1-3-1.note_es: Una pregunta de sí/no se convierte en indirecta con if o whether. El orden vuelve a ser sujeto + verbo.

B1-3-1.title: Past question to indirect: whether
B1-3-1.note_es: Con did, el auxiliar desaparece y el verbo pasa a pasado: Did he call? se convierte en I wonder whether he called.

B1-5-0.title: Noun + relative clause
B1-5-0.note_es: Un nombre general (the kind of..., someone, anything) se completa con una cláusula relativa que lo describe.

B1-5-1.point: Expectations: it’s the custom to, (not) supposed to, expected to, (not) acceptable to
B1-5-1.title: Expectation patterns
B1-5-1.note_es: Todas estas frases expresan lo que se espera socialmente y van seguidas de to + verbo base.

B1-6-0.point: Describing problems with past participles as adjectives and with nouns
B1-6-0.title: Participle to problem noun
B1-6-0.note_es: Un problema se puede decir con un participio (is cracked) o con un nombre (there’s a crack in...).

B1-6-1.point: Need + gerund, need + passive infinitive, and keep + gerund
B1-6-1.title: Need + gerund = need + passive infinitive
B1-6-1.note_es: Las dos formas tienen el mismo significado: algo necesita ser arreglado. Con -ing es activa en forma pero pasiva en sentido.

B1-6-1.title: Keep + gerund
B1-6-1.note_es: Keep + -ing describe algo que se repite o no para, y suele molestar.

B1-7-0.point: Passive in the present continuous and present perfect; prepositions of cause
B1-7-0.title: Passive: being repaired vs have been replaced
B1-7-0.note_es: Is being + participio: la acción ocurre ahora. Have been + participio: ya ocurrió y el resultado se ve ahora.

B1-7-1.title: Purpose: same subject or different subject
B1-7-1.note_es: Si quien hace la acción es el mismo sujeto, usa to + verbo. Si es otra persona, añade for + persona antes de to + verbo.

columns.head: to + verb
columns.use_es: Quien actúa es quien tiene el objetivo.

items.t: We closed the bay to carry out repairs.
I called to confirm the time.

columns.head: for + object + to + verb
columns.use_es: Otra persona hace la acción final.

items.t: We closed the bay for the engineers to work.
We stopped for the crew to rest.

B1-8-0.title: Would rather vs would prefer
B1-8-0.note_es: Would rather va con verbo base, sin to. Would prefer va con to + verbo o con un nombre. Con otra persona: I’d rather you didn’t.

columns.head: would prefer
columns.use_es: Con to, o con un nombre.

B1-8-1.point: By + gerund to describe how to do things
B1-8-1.title: By + gerund = how
B1-8-1.note_es: By + verbo con -ing explica cómo se logra el resultado. En negativo: by not + -ing.

B1-9-0.title: Have something done
B1-9-0.note_es: Have/get + objeto + participio: otra persona hace la acción por ti. El agente no se menciona. Get es más informal.

B1-9-1.point: Making suggestions with modals, gerunds, negative questions and infinitives
B1-9-1.title: Ways to make suggestions
B1-9-1.note_es: Cada fórmula pide una estructura distinta: modal + verbo, How about + -ing, pregunta negativa y it might be worth + -ing.

B1-11-0.point: Time clauses: before, after, once, the moment, as soon as, until, by the time
B1-11-0.title: Time clauses: future vs past
B1-11-0.note_es: Para el futuro, la cláusula de tiempo usa presente (nunca will). Para el pasado, by the time + pasado simple lleva pasado perfecto en la otra oración.

columns.head: future
columns.use_es: As soon as / once / until + presente.

items.t: As soon as I finish, I’ll send it.
Once I’ve finished, I’ll send it.
As soon as I will finish, I’ll send it.
After I sent it, she called.
By the time we arrived, the train had left.

B1-12-0.point: Describing purpose with infinitive clauses and with for
B1-12-0.title: Purpose patterns
B1-12-0.note_es: Para el propósito usa to, in order to o so as to + verbo. En negativo: in order not to. Si cambia el sujeto: for + persona + to + verbo.

B1-12-1.point: Giving reasons with because, since, because of, for, due to and the reason
B1-12-1.title: Giving reasons
B1-12-1.note_es: Because y since van con una cláusula. Because of y due to van con un nombre. The reason is that introduce una explicación completa.

items.t: We stopped because the pump failed.
Since nobody replied, I made the decision myself.
We stopped because of the failure.
We stopped due to a pump failure.
We stopped due to the pump failed.
The reason is that the pump failed.
The reason for the delay was a failure.
The reason is because the pump failed.

B1-13-0.point: Past modals for degrees of certainty
B1-13-0.title: Past certainty with modals
B1-13-0.note_es: Estos modales + have + participio expresan cuánta certeza tienes sobre algo del pasado.

marks.ex: It might have been the sensor.

B1-13-1.point: Past modals for judgments and suggestions
B1-13-1.title: Judging the past with modals
B1-13-1.note_es: Se usa modal + have + participio para juzgar lo que pasó: should (crítica), could (otra opción posible) y would (lo que tú harías).

items.t: They should have run a second test.
We could have caught it earlier.

B1-14-0.point: The passive to describe a process
B1-14-0.title: Describing a process with the passive
B1-14-0.note_es: En un proceso importa la acción, no quién la hace. Usa is/are + participio y secuenciadores como first, then, finally.

steps.ex: The parts are cleaned in three baths.
Each unit is tested for leaks.
The units are packed and shipped.

B1-14-1.title: Defining vs non-defining clauses
B1-14-1.note_es: La cláusula definitoria identifica al nombre y no lleva comas. La no definitoria añade información extra, va entre comas y no admite that.

columns.head: defining
columns.use_es: Sin comas. Who, that o which.

items.t: The engineer who signed it has left.
The machine that failed is old.
Ana, who signed it, has left.
The machine, which is ten years old, failed.
Ana, that signed it, has left.

B1-15-0.point: Recommendations and opinions with passive modals
B1-15-0.title: Passive modals: how strong?
B1-15-0.note_es: Los modales en pasiva (modal + be + participio) dan desde una idea tentativa hasta una obligación fuerte.

marks.ex: This has got to be fixed.

B1-15-1.title: Tag questions: the sign flips
B1-15-1.note_es: La coletilla pide confirmar una opinión. Si la oración es afirmativa, la coletilla es negativa; si es negativa, la coletilla es afirmativa. Usa el mismo auxiliar.

pairs.hint_es: Verbo to be: se repite is.
Presente simple: el auxiliar es do.
Con modal, se repite el modal.
Pasado de to be: se repite was.

B1-16-0.point: Accomplishments with the simple past and present perfect
B1-16-0.title: Accomplishments: finished time or open period
B1-16-0.note_es: Con un momento terminado (in May, last month) usa pasado simple. Con un periodo abierto (so far, this year) usa presente perfecto.

examples.t: I passed my driving test in May.
I’ve completed four modules so far.

B1-16-1.point: Goals with the future perfect and would like to have + past participle
B1-16-1.title: Goals: future perfect
B1-16-1.note_es: Will have + participio dice que algo estará terminado antes de un momento futuro. Would like to have + participio expresa un deseo sobre algo hecho para entonces.

examples.t: By June, I’ll have finished the course.
I’d like to have travelled more by then.
